dervis-irab:1-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَضُحاها) al-Qurṭubī said: "(الضحى) is feminine. One says (ارتفعت الضحى) 'the forenoon rose', above (الضحو); it is also treated as masculine. Whoever treats it as feminine takes it to be the plural of (ضحوة); whoever treats it as masculine takes it to be a noun of the pattern fuʿal, like (صرد)." Ibn Khālawayh said: "(الضحى) is a shortened noun like (هدى). (الضحى) is feminine, and its diminutive is (ضحية); but the better course is to say (ضحيّ) in its diminutive without the hāʾ, so that its diminutive does not resemble the diminutive of (ضحوة). (الضحى) is the face of the day. One says (ليلة اضحيان) when the moon in it is bright from its beginning to its end. (أضحى النهار) means the day rose. One says (ضحي فلان للشمس يضحى) when he came out to the sun and appeared. Allah the Exalted said: (وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى). Ibn ʿUmar saw a man saying the talbiya in a hidden voice and said to him: (أضح لمن لبّيت له), that is, make it evident. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
رأت رجلا أيما إذا الشمس عارضت ... فيضحى وأيما بالعشيّ فيخصر
(She saw a man who, whenever the sun met him, would come out into the open, and who in the evening would be chilled.)"
And in al-Qāmūs: "(الضّحو) and (الضحوة) and (الضّحية), like (عشيّة), is the rising of the day; (الضحى) is a little after it; it is treated as masculine and its diminutive is (ضحيّ) without a hāʾ; (الضحاء), with a long vowel, is when midday draws near; with ḍamma and shortened, [it is the same]; (أتيتك ضحوة وضحى) 'I came to you in the forenoon'; (أضحى) means he entered it, and he made a thing appear; (ضاحاه) means he came to him in it."
(جَلَّاها) He made it appear and uncovered it.
(طَحاها) He spread it out, because what appears of it to the beholder is like a carpet, so this does not conflict with its being spherical. In al-Mukhtār: "(طحاه) means he spread it out, like (دحاه), and its pattern is (عدا)." And in al-Qāmūs: "(طحا يطحو) means he went far away and perished, and he threw a man on his face. (الطحا) is the level stretch of land. (طحى), like (سعى), means he spread out, and was spread out, and lay down, and went away in the land. (طحا به قلبه) means his heart carried him off into every matter."
(دَسَّاها) (التدسية) is diminishing and concealing through immorality. The origin of (دسى) is (دسس), as was said of (تقضض) that it became (تقضى), and as was said (قصيت أظفاري), whose origin is (قصصت أظفاري).
(فَدَمْدَمَ) He closed the punishment over them for their sin and destroyed them. al-Farrāʾ said: "The reality of (الدمدمة) is the doubling and repeating of punishment. One says (دمدمت على الشيء) when you covered it over." In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "(دمدمت الشيء) is when you made it stick to the ground; (دمدم الله عليهم) means Allah destroyed them; one says (دمدمت على الميت التراب) meaning I levelled it over him." Ibn al-Anbārī said: "(دمدم) means he became angry, and (الدمدمة) is speech that alarms a man." In al-Qāmūs: "(دمم الأرض) means he levelled it; (دمم فلانا) means he punished him with a complete punishment; and (دمم القوم) means he destroyed them, like (دهدم) and (دمدم عليهم)."
(عُقْباها) Its consequence and its outcome. In al-Qāmūs: "(أعقبه الله بطاعته) means He rewarded him, and (العقبى) is the recompense of a matter."

* I'rab:
(وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحاها وَالْقَمَرِ إِذا تَلاها)
The wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; (الشمس) is genitive through the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb of the oath. (وضحاها) is conjoined to (الشمس); (والقمر) is likewise conjoined. (إذا) is for mere time, attached to the omitted verb of the oath. An objection has been raised that the verb of the oath is a performative (inshāʾ) whose time is the present, so it cannot govern (إذا), since that is for the future, and a difference of time between the governing word and the governed is necessarily impossible. It was answered that it is permissible to swear now by the rising of a star in the future, so the oath is in the present and the rising in the future; and it is permissible to swear by a future thing, as you say "I swear by Allah, when the sun rises", where the oath becomes binding at the sun's rising. The verb of the oath is of the present only when it does not depend on a condition. We have set this out usefully and fully in the discussion of Sūrat al-Takwīr. The clause (تلاها) is in the position of a genitive, as the adverb is annexed to it.
(وَالنَّهارِ إِذا جَلَّاها وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَغْشاها)
The two clauses are strung onto what preceded and parallel it in i'rab.
(وَالسَّماءِ وَما بَناها وَالْأَرْضِ وَما طَحاها)
Likewise conjoined. (ما) in the three clauses is either maṣdar or in the sense of (من), and in any case it is conjoined to the noun before it, or the interpreted maṣdar formed from it and the verb is conjoined to it. al-Zamakhsharī rejected its being maṣdar.
(وَنَفْسٍ وَما سَوَّاها)
Likewise strung onto what preceded. The indefiniteness in (نفس) is meant for the genus, as though He had said "and any one of the souls".
(فَأَلْهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْواها)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; (ألهمها) is a past verb with a latent agent and a direct object; (فجورها) is a second direct object; and (وتقواها) is conjoined to (فجورها). They differed over the meaning of inspiration (ilhām). Ibn Jubayr said: "He made it incumbent upon it." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "He made it known to it." Ibn Zayd said: "He made it clear to it." al-Zajjāj said: "He granted it success towards piety, and 'He inspired it with its immorality' means He forsook it." It was also said: He made it known to it and gave it a power with which both the acquisition of immorality and the acquisition of piety are possible. al-Zamakhsharī said:
"The meaning of inspiring immorality and piety is making it understand and comprehend that one of them is good and the other ugly, and enabling it to choose whichever of them it wishes." In this is an allusion to the doctrine of the Muʿtazila, who hold rational good and evil (al-taḥsīn wa-l-taqbīḥ al-ʿaqliyyān), that is, that good and evil are perceived by reason. The Sunnis, however, hold legal (revealed) good and evil, that is, that good and evil are perceived only through revelation, because they return to the legal rulings, without discarding the role of reason in perceiving the legal rulings; and in their view the knowledge of every legal ruling requires two premises: a rational one, which leads to the creed, and a revealed one built upon it, which indicates the specific ruling.
As for inspiration (al-ilhām) in the language, it is the casting of something into the mind. al-Rāghib said: "It is specific to what comes from the side of the Exalted and the side of the Highest Assembly. The Exalted said: (فألهمها فجورها وتقواها), so it is known that it is not specific to good but includes evil as well." In technical usage it is the casting of a meaning into the heart by way of outpouring without acquisition, so it is specific to good, since "outpouring" is not applied to evil, for which "whispering" (waswasa) is used.
(قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاها وَقَدْ خابَ مَنْ دَسَّاها)
The clause is the answer to the oath, and the lām was omitted because of the length of the speech. It was also said that the answer is omitted, its implied form being "you will surely be resurrected". al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its implied form is 'Allah will surely destroy them', meaning the people of Mecca, for their denial of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as He destroyed Thamūd because they denied Ṣāliḥ. As for (قد أفلح), it is speech following His saying (فألهمها فجورها وتقواها) by way of digression, and is not part of the answer to the oath at all." (قد) is a particle of certainty; (أفلح) is a past verb; (من) is a relative noun, the agent; the clause (زكّاها) is the ṣila; and the agent of (زكاها) is a pronoun returning to (من). It was also said that it is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "he has succeeded whom Allah the Exalted has purified through obedience". (وقد خاب من دسّاها) is conjoined to the preceding clause and parallel to it.
(كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْواها إِذِ انْبَعَثَ أَشْقاها)
A resumptive statement, delivered to confirm what was mentioned about the success of the one who purified his soul, or whom Allah purified, and the failure of the one who corrupted his soul, or whom Allah corrupted. (كذبت ثمود): a past verb and an agent; (بطغواها), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (كذبت). The meaning of the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "because of their transgression". In al-Kashshāf he made it for seeking aid, figuratively, as in your saying "I wrote with the pen", meaning: they did the denying by means of their transgression. Both (الطغوى) and (الطغيان) are verbal nouns, but the expression with (الطغوى) was chosen because it better resembles the ends of the verses. In al-Mukhtār: "(طغى يطغى), with fatḥa on the ghayn in both, and (يطغو), (طغيانا) and (طغوانا), mean he exceeded the limit; (طغي), with kasra, is the same; and (الطغوى), with fatḥa, is like (الطغيان)." As for al-Zamakhsharī, he said: "(الطغوى) is from (الطغيان). They distinguished between the noun and the adjective in the pattern fuʿlā from the roots ending in yāʾ, by turning the yāʾ into wāw in the noun and leaving it unchanged in the adjective, and so they said (امرأة خزيا) and (صديا)." (إذ) is an adverb for the time past, attached to (كذبت) or to (الطغوى); the clause (انبعث) is in the position of a genitive, as the adverb is annexed to it; and (أشقاها) is the agent of (انبعث). What is meant by it is Qudār ibn Sālif, with ḍamma on the qāf, who is made a proverb for ill omen, so it is said "more ill-omened than Qudār"; he was nicknamed "the red one of Thamūd". It is also permissible that they were a group, and the singular is because the elative, when annexed, is the same for singular and plural, masculine and feminine. The wording of Ibn Khālawayh, in which he made a strange confusion, is: "If the masculine is (أشقى), then the woman is (شقواء), because it is of the wāw-class, as in His saying: (ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا) and (شقاوتنا). The (ها) is genitive by annexation. The plural of (أشقى) is (شقو), like (حمر) and (صفر); if you form a sound plural you say (أشقون) in the masculine and (شقواوات) in the feminine, like (حمراوات)." Ibn Hishām said in reply: "His saying 'if the masculine is (أشقى) the feminine is (شقواء) and the plural (شقو)' is not good, as he did not distinguish between the afʿal that is an adjective of an indefinite noun and the afʿal that follows the course of nouns and is an adjective of an indefinite noun only with (من), being either annexed or accompanied by (أل). The feminine in this case is (الشقيا), and the masculine plural is (الأشقون), and (الأشاقي) is permissible by analogy, just as you say (الأكبر), (الأكبرون) and (الأكابر); and the feminine plural is (الشّقى) and (الشقييات), just as you say (الكبرى), (الكبر) and (الكبريات)."
(فَقالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ناقَةَ اللَّهِ وَسُقْياها)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; (قال) is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; (لهم), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (قال); (رسول الله) is the agent; and (ناقة الله) is accusative as a warning (taḥdhīr) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "leave off hamstringing her and beware of her drinking". A discussion of the warning will come in the section on Benefits. (وسقياها) is conjoined to (ناقة الله), i.e. "and her turn of drinking".
(فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوها فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنْبِهِمْ فَسَوَّاها وَلا يَخافُ عُقْباها)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; (كذبوه) is a verb, an agent and a direct object. (فعقروها) is conjoined to (فكذبوه), i.e. Qudār struck her on her legs and brought her down, and they slaughtered her and divided her meat among themselves. (فدمدم) is likewise conjoined; (عليهم), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (دمدم); (ربهم) is the agent; and (بذنبهم) is also attached to (دمدم), the bāʾ being causal, i.e. "because of their sin". (فسوّاها) is conjoined to (دمدم). The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is negative; (يخاف عقباها) is an imperfect verb, with a latent agent and a direct object. We made the wāw a conjunction only to suit the reading with the fāʾ, which is also one of the Seven; although the parsers and the commentators say that the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive; among those who said it is a conjunction is Ibn Khālawayh.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying (ولا يخاف عقباها) there is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), on the view that the pronoun in (يخاف) refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which is the apparent sense: that He, Glory be to Him, does not fear its consequence, as kings fear the consequence of their deeds. The purpose of the metaphor is to humiliate and abase them. It is also permissible that the pronoun return to the Messenger, i.e. that he does not fear the consequence of his warning them, and the metaphor remains. al-Suddī, Muqātil, al-Zajjāj and Abū ʿAlī said: the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl and the pronoun in (يخاف) returns to (أشقاها), i.e. he rose up to hamstring her while not fearing the outcome of his act, because of his disbelief and transgression. (العقبى) is the end of a thing and what comes of matters in its wake. In this there is some remoteness, because of the length of the interval between the ḥāl and its owner.

* Benefits:
The warning (al-taḥdhīr): it is the putting of a noun in the accusative by an omitted verb that conveys alerting and warning, the verb being implied as suits the situation, such as "beware", "keep away", "avoid", "guard against", "protect yourself" and the like. The warning is:
1- Sometimes with the word (إياك) and its derivatives, as in (إياك والكذب): (إياك) is an overt detached pronoun in the position of the accusative as the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "keep away" or "guard against" or "beware"; and (الكذب) is conjoined to (إياك), or is a direct object of an omitted verb as well, as before. You may also make the wāw one of accompaniment and (الكذب) a mafʿūl maʿahu.
2- Sometimes without (إياك) and its derivatives, as in (نفسك والشر) and (الأسد الأسد); their i'rab is as before.
3- Sometimes with the word (إياه) and (إياي) and their derivatives, when conjoined to the one warned, as in his saying:
فلا تصحب أخا الجهل ... وإياك وإياه
(So do not keep company with the ignorant man, and beware of yourself and him.)
The governing verb in a warning is necessarily omitted in three places:
1- That the thing warned with is (إياك) itself and its derivatives.
2- That there is a conjunction.
3- That there is repetition, as in your saying: (الأسد الأسد).
It is strange that al-Nasafī mentioned in his commentary that the saying of the Exalted (ناقة الله وسقياها) is an incitement (ighrāʾ). There is no doubt of its problematic nature on the apparent reading, because incitement does not apply to it on the apparent reading; what applies to it is only the warning.
